title: Importance of Earning Through Labor
summary: The hadith emphasizes the virtue of earning through one's own efforts rather than relying on others.
translation: In earning, a person who earns his livelihood through his own labor and then feeds himself and his family holds great virtue. Islam has always encouraged this practice, indicating that relying on someone else's mercy or hope signifies weakness, which Islam disapproves of. Thus, many encouragements are mentioned in the noble Hadith. Listen to one Hadith of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), who says, 'One of you gathers a bundle of wood on his back and then sells it, which is better for him than asking someone who might give or not give.' Therefore, scholars say that earning is sometimes obligatory, sometimes forbidden, sometimes recommended, and sometimes permissible. It is obligatory when it meets the necessary needs of the earner and their family. It is forbidden when earned for pride and ostentation. It is recommended when one earns more than the need with the intention of giving the surplus to the poor, needy, and relatives. It is permissible when one earns more than necessary to maintain one's dignity and status while staying within the bounds of Sharia. It is mentioned about Prophet David (peace be upon him) that he used to eat from his hand's labor. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said that Prophet David (peace be upon him) used to earn through his own labor to eat.
